summary.headline: Allcargo Terminals Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR47 crore (vs INR35 crore YoY) on 7.2% TEU growth to 1,76,499 TEUs.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR214 crore, up from INR187 crore a year earlier and INR208 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA excluding other income was INR47 crore, with management citing yield management, technology-led efficiencies and higher transhipment share. PAT fell to INR6 crore from INR9 crore, hit by tax on dividend from JV companies and a prior-year tax item. Management also announced a leadership change, with Pranav Choudhary replacing Suresh Kumar as MD from September 1, 2026.

segments.name: Container handling (CFS, EXIM)
segments.commentary: Volumes 1,76,499 TEUs, up 7.2% YoY; imports are 75-80% of CFS volumes. Annual handling capacity rose ~20% in FY26 to ~1.03 million TEUs (~10.1 lakh TEU per management).

segments.name: LCL business for Allcargo Group
segments.commentary: Close to 10-12% of revenue from handling LCL containers for Allcargo Logistics at JNPA, Mundra and Chennai; margins said to be similar to third-party business.

segments.name: Nepal JV
segments.commentary: Operates one ICD and three ICPs with a Nepal partner; contributes about 2-3% of overall revenue and profitability.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA per TEU expected to stay around INR2,400 going forward (CFO); management later guided to INR2,400-2,500 range.
3-year plan (Plan 2030) targets EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750 including Farukhnagar, and capacity of 13 lakh TEUs / ~1 million TEU operator.
Tax rate expected at 25% going forward under the concessional regime.
No dividend at present; management says it will move to regular dividends once projects are funded and cash flows are covered, timing not given.
Management expects ICDs to add a natural profitability uplift in ~1.5 years; without it, profitability expected to hover around current levels given competition.
capex_capacity: Plan 2030 capex estimate ~INR400 crore covering Farukhnagar, Speedy JNPA expansion, Mundra and Chennai; ~INR100 crore expected to be spent in FY27.

Funding: INR120 crore equity raised recently (INR25 crore called, ~INR90 crore yet to be called); ~INR50 crore internal accruals; ~INR70 crore annual business cash flow; debt of INR100-150 crore with banks already tied up.

Speedy JNPA: ~60,000 TEU addition after 10-year renewal; tender done, work to start post-monsoon, completion by Jan-Feb 2027; ~INR20 crore capex in FY27. JNPA facility upgrade of INR40 crore co-funded 50:50 with JNPA.

Farukhnagar PFT: completion targeted Feb-Mar 2027 (standalone PFT initially, domestic focus); ICD portion by Oct-Dec 2027. Management says PFT volumes will be 20-25% domestic and 75-80% EXIM once ICD is operational.

Chennai (Kattupalli cluster): site identification in advanced negotiations; firm timeline expected next quarter. Mundra: land acquired; decision on extension with landlord or a larger facility to be taken during the year (current licence to 2030-31).
Capacity utilisation at ~80-85% (vs 60-65% three years ago); Chennai and one Mundra facility fully utilised. Capacity rising from 8.3 lakh to 13 lakh TEUs by 2030 vision.
Smart yard management system piloted at JNPT, the largest facility; myCFS app automates ~70% of the 14-15 step import workflow, with export work being added.
demand_pricing: Average realisation up to ~INR13,000 per TEU from ~INR11,000-11,500 a year earlier, driven by yield management, better selling practices and a recent rate increase.
Management attributes the EBITDA per TEU improvement roughly 50:50 to yield management and operational efficiencies (RST modernisation, yard management systems).
Higher transhipment share and favourable cargo mix (ODC, reefer, container size) cited as margin drivers.
Pan-India scale has reduced transport, equipment and security costs; input cost increases (fuel, transporter contracts) absorbed through rate changes.
Management says the market is very competitive and further yield gains beyond current levels are limited.
Rail and DFC: Mundra's rail coefficient is high; JNPA rail share has room to improve. Allcargo Terminals holds ~7.5% in HORCL and expects preferential DFCC access in ~1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Raj Doshi asked for capex plans for FY27 and FY28 and how funding splits between internal accruals and debt.
qa_highlights.answer: Plan 2030 capex is about INR400 crore covering Farukhnagar, Speedy JNPA, Mundra and Chennai, with about INR100 crore in FY27. Funding is INR120 crore equity (INR25 crore called, about INR90 crore yet to be called), about INR50 crore accruals, about INR70 crore annual cash flow, and INR100-150 crore of bank debt already tied up.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA per TEU target applies once the ICD is operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is maintaining about INR2,400 per TEU, and the 3-year plan targets INR2,750 per TEU including Farukhnagar, where rail revenue will add to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Does the group send business to Allcargo Terminals, and how do DFC and rail affect the ICD business?
qa_highlights.answer: LCL handling for Allcargo Logistics is about 10-12% of revenue at JNPA, Mundra and Chennai, at margins similar to third-party business. Mundra has a high rail coefficient, JNPA has room to improve, and the company holds about 7.5% of HORCL, which should give preferential DFCC access in 1-1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin of about 22% sustainable, and what is the guidance for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited commercial yield management, cargo mix and pan-India cost savings, with capacity utilisation up to 80-85% from 60-65% three years ago. Without ICDs, EBITDA per TEU should hover at current levels, with a guided range of INR2,400-2,500, as the market is very competitive and further yield gains are limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why no dividend despite a cash-rich business, and is there a payout policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend for now; cash is being prioritised for funding projects after a recent equity raise and three years since listing. Management says it will move to regular dividends once projects are funded and cash flows are covered, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise, and is it a run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise reflects annual increments of about 10% and about INR1 crore of ESOP cost for the CEO in the quarter. Management said the quarterly level can be treated as a regular run rate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines for Chennai and Farukhnagar commercialisation, and is FY27 growth limited to current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Speedy JNPA work starts post-monsoon with completion by Jan-Feb 2027. Farukhnagar PFT is due Feb-Mar 2027 and the ICD by Oct-Dec 2027. Chennai site is in advanced talks with a firm timeline next quarter, and Mundra's landlord extension decision is due this year. Management agreed FY27 growth relies on current capacity, with new capacity ramping from next year.

qa_highlights.question: How does myCFS work and how widely is it adopted?
qa_highlights.answer: myCFS automates about 70% of the 14-15 step import workflow, with export work being added. CHA monthly usage is 70-80% among the large CHAs it targets, and management believes only 2-3 other CFSs among about 140 have a similar solution.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA per TEU gain came from pricing versus cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation rose to about INR13,000 per TEU from INR11,000-11,500 a year earlier, and attributed the margin gain roughly 50:50 to yield management and operational efficiencies such as RST modernisation and yard systems.

risks_watch: Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on yield gains that management says are nearing a limit in a very competitive market, with guidance of INR2,400-2,500 per TEU.
Execution risk on capex of about INR400 crore, with Farukhnagar PFT due Feb-Mar 2027 and ICD due Oct-Dec 2027, and Speedy JNPA expansion due Jan-Feb 2027.
Funding: about INR90 crore of the INR120 crore equity is yet to be called, and INR100-150 crore of debt is planned.
Chennai site is not yet firm (timeline promised next quarter); Mundra extension versus a larger facility decision is pending this year.
Leadership transition: Pranav Choudhary takes over as MD from September 1, 2026, replacing Suresh Kumar.
PAT pressure from tax on JV dividends, prior-year tax and the shift to a 25% tax rate; monitor PAT against EBITDA growth.
No dividend policy yet; timing of regular dividends is not given.
key_quotes: Even without that, we expect the profitability numbers to hover around the current level because as you know, the market is very competitive.
We have also introduced technology in the form of myCFS, which more which is more in terms of customer convenience rather than any direct impact on the cost.

As we execute our projects, as we go into the different trajectory where the cash flow requirements have been fully taken care of and we are good invested into a project, we will look at those -- returning some of this money to our investors by way of dividend.
So overall, there is a requirement of close to INR400 crores of capex.
summary.management_tone: Confident on capacity, technology and the 1 million TEU, 3-year ambition, but cautious on pricing headroom, saying the market is very competitive and yield gains are close to their limit. Evasive on dividend timing and on the Chennai site, which is still under negotiation with no firm date.
